title: Godot devs, what does your AI pipeline look like currently?
author: OMBERX
selftext:
Hello!  I'm very new to AI tools.  The most experience I have with it at the moment is asking ChatGPT a question in the browser, and that's about it.  I've been a software developer for 4 years working mainly in Angular, but we don't really use AI tools at the company I work at, so I'm really ignorant to everything.

Godot is my main game engine.  I've been a hobbyist game dev for \~7 years now, and primarily used Unity until the whole license debacle.

My question to you guys is, what does your AI pipeline look like?  I'm looking for specifics if possible like what AI you are using, what plan, how to set it up, etc.  I only want to use it for code, I don't care about generating art nor do I want to.

comments.author: mggriebz
comments.body: Use codex —> ask how to setup/test Godot MCP -> follow any responses back from codex chat - > ask if to test/validate it can launch and run godot tests -> start vibing

replies.author: sircontagious
replies.body: Dont use an mcp with godot, it makes no sense.

replies.author: mggriebz
replies.body: From my experience it helped verify and create the tests through my codex sessions so I guess it made sense to me at the time

replies.author: sircontagious
replies.body: Did you have experience with programming or godot before ai? MCPs do not make sense for godot because everything is in text format. Agents can edit files with complete sanity without adding the significantly slower layer of going through a hosted service. The services are best for things like unreal or unity that make heavy usage of binaries that are difficult for the agents to parse.

replies.author: IriFlina
replies.body: How would an agent take screenshots of the game typically?

replies.author: sircontagious
replies.body: Very easily. There are a million ways to grab an image from the active window. Two ways exist within godot itself; an active screenshot and movie maker mode. It can do both via the command line or script without an mcp. Dont waste your money. Just open a claude window right now and ask it to take a picture of something in game.

replies.author: mggriebz
replies.body: Ok I think that makes sense… I guess all I can speak from is personal experience which is that when I asked codex/claude to use and install the free MCP, it seemed to run and create better tests.

replies.author: Weaves87
replies.body:
The confusing thing to me is that there are multiple MCP servers for Godot right now.

Based on my research there’s one in particular which sounds like it is best (it’s an editor plugin), but it’s not the top search result when you search “Godot MCP” on Google - so it’s all the more confusing

What kinds of issues have you run into and which MCP server are you using?

Godot is obviously text based so it naturally works pretty well for the AI to iterate on code/resources/scenes, but the challenge seems to be creating that full autonomous loop where the AI can launch the game, issue keystrokes to control things, and snap screenshots, etc

replies.author: sircontagious
replies.body: It can do literally all of that without an mcp. Skills make sense if you want to make it more reliable. An mcp does not. I put more info in another comment.

replies.author: Weaves87
replies.body:
Took a read thru your comments, makes sense. Ties back to Godot being very much text-based.

The thing about my use case is that I prefer having the agent locked down in a VM inside of my Windows box (via WSL), and allowing it to control Godot outside of the VM. That way I don’t have to allow the agent to have unfettered access to the rest of my PC

I mentioned this when consulting with Claude on it and it sounds like the editor plugin MCP can allow that to happen. I still think I may give that a whirl and at least test that out

replies.author: _playlogic_
replies.body:
None of what he said makes sense. He is just repeating a something he has yet to prove his “MCPs are evil” rhetoric. My suggestion is that you do research yourself and even try them yourself. Not all MCPs are the same, some don’t even use the protocol and are really CLIs similar to the Unity CLI. Just think for a moment…Yes Godot is text based, but that means the Agent needs to read your entire file using either “sed” or it read tool to take action. 

Yes MCP and CLI were terrible in the past, but things have improved just like the agents that use them. The issue is people keep parroting  the same narrative without going to update their knowledge.

comments.author: tastethecrainbow
comments.body:
Get Claude Code or Antigravity or any other CLI tool and use them in the godot directory. I use Claude code and Matt Pocock skills like wayfinder and grill with docs to make decisions, plan and build task tickets against my git repo and then have short sessions in claude code or antigravity to implement and build tests for them. I've found Claude Opus or even Sonnet generally effective at coding and building UI and deeper engine stuff when given enough prep and discussion to make sure we're building the right thing. Antigravity with 3.8 Flash has been good for smaller tasks and tweaks and just open ended discussion where all I want to do is make issues in the repo or discussion features in my project. A combination of the two with good skills has made my work fairly easy. 

Going back and forth in a chat is a time and token sink with rapidly diminishing returns and it's a futile effort for anything more complex than tic tac toe

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body: This is exactly my workflow with Godot and I’ve been having great success with it.

replies.body: Thank you for the suggestion!  Claude Code seems like the best option from what most people have said so I'll probably do that. Does that make sense?

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
Get a Claude Code sub, point it at the directory, and tell it what to implement. Use Opus 5.5 medium for most work. Ask it to tell you its plan first if you want, that way you can get an idea. Have a sonnet or a chatgpt model review the change.

These days I do all of my development on the Claude mobile app. Just set up the cloud sandbox and your GitHub repo and let it make changes, it's awesome.

replies.body: How are these sprites in comparison to a paid service like Pixellab? I've been using pixellab for a month and having Claude use it with API access to generate sprites for me. It gives really good results

replies.body: I would say they are decent. The results are fine 9 out of 10 times. Also it depends on the type of game that you are trying to develop. For me it is an rts style fast wave shooter with a higher camera angle. So minor differences between the sprites doesn't matter much for me.

comments.body:

The latter is counter intuitive but it has helped it from running away and making wrong decisions on things I want more hands on.

comments.author: beta_1457
comments.body:
I use Antigravity IDE with 3.8 flash.

I have a coding standards document that it references and I force it to use. Like making sure to have strict typing. \*Note: sometimes it just ignores my coding standards and I have to remind it still, then it will fix it.

But I find giving it smaller tasks works very well.

For larger tasks I build out an implementation plan and execute the steps 1 at a time.

I've been using Godot for almost 4 years now and am very comfortable scripting in GDscript, I find using the AI agent a great augmentation tool. I can maintain my good architecture/coding standards but do everything a lot faster. I rebuilt my entire project I was working on the last few years in the last 8 weeks and it's honestly... a lot better.

My little brother even told me, "No offense, but this looks like sometime I'd actually play compared to your last game." It's been a lot faster to implement my vision and get to unit testing.

comments.author: Short_Stable2397
comments.body:
Disclosure: I am building a Godot MCP.

A lot of comments saying no need for MCP because Godot is text based, agents can already take screenshots etc. From my experience the error rate without MCP is still higher. The agent doesn't proactively close the testing loop on its own without the right tools being offered. They tend to simply stop and tell you to try it out.

MCPs can provide that framework. It saves you time going back and forth because each extra turn of 'you got this little bit wrong' costs tokens. Why not give the agent something that would help it work better? Yes MCP tools cost context. Obviously I think the trade off is worth it.
